verdict.rationale: Restate documents a single self-contained binary with no external dependencies that runs on a local machine, plus a TypeScript testing companion library that runs a Restate Server via Testcontainers to test handlers. That covers local engine startup and integration-style testing, but nothing shows time skipping or mocked steps for unit tests. missing for 10: time-skipping test support, mocked step/ctx.run utilities, an explicit single-command local start, testing utilities for other SDKs, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a backend developer, one command runs the whole engine locally, and testing utilities let me unit-test workflows with time skipping and mocked steps

citations.quote: Restate is a single self-contained binary. No external dependencies needed.
making it easy to run it on a variety of platforms, from your local machine, to a VM, to Kubernetes
This uses [Testcontainers](https://testcontainers.com/) to run a Restate Server in a Docker container and let you test your Restate handlers.
The Typescript SDK has a companion library which makes it easy to test against a Restate container
